Q: How can I install packages using pip according to the requirements.txt file from a local directory? A:

Use pip3 install -r requirements.txt. But make sure the requirements.txt file has been pulled from origin and not added to file .gitignore.

Q: Is javascript capable of recursively querying a website? A:

Besides using NodeJS it's possible to use JavaScript in cloud platforms like Google Apps Script.

Google Apps Script includes the URL Fetch Service to make HTTP requests. It has limitations compared to other options available in the wild but it can be used to do HTTP GET request to fetch a web page if that page has not implemented measures to block automated requests.

If the web page source code is sucessfully retrieved, the next step will be to parse the content. Please bear in mind that since the code runs on the server side most Web APIs, like Document, are not available. One option is to use the Google Apps Script library CheerioGS.

Q: Excel VBA file copy external to excel A:

I think it's difficult to reflect the results of xcopy in the sheet.

I created a sample in VBScript that copies and reflects the results onto a sheet.

If the workbook is already open, it will be opened as Read-Only.

Since I cannot write to the workbook that is open, I am saving it under a different name.

Also, if it is displayed from the beginning, you can scroll, but selecting a cell causes the script to error.

Therefore, it is being run in hidden mode.

If an error occurs while hidden, the Excel process remains running, so I modified it in JScript to catch the error and display the sheet.

Unlike VBA, VBScript has commands and functions that cannot be used.

Debugging might be difficult, but if you'd like, please give it a try.

VBSSample.wsf

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes" ?>
<package>
  <job id="run">
    <reference object="Scripting.FileSystemObject"/>  <!-- When using FileSystemObject -->
    <reference object="Scripting.Dictionary"/>        <!-- When using Dictionary -->
<!--  Execution order
         VBScript -- JScript -- RunVBProcess -->
    <script language="VBScript"><![CDATA[
      Option Explicit

      WScript.Echo("start")
      Dim FSO
      Dim ExcelApp
      Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
      Set ExcelApp = CreateObject("Excel.Application")
      ExcelApp.Visible = false

      Public Sub RunVBProcess()
          Dim wb
          Dim ws
          Dim bookPath
          Dim Outputsheet
          Dim irow
          Dim strInDir
          Dim strInPath
          Dim strOutDir
          Dim strOutPath
          Dim strSavePath
          Dim strNow

          bookPath = "C:\Temp\Book1.xlsx"
          Set wb = ExcelApp.Workbooks.Open(bookPath,,True)
          Set Outputsheet = wb.Sheets("Sheet1")
          strInDir = "C:\Temp\In"
          strOutDir = "C:\Temp\Out"

          For irow = 1 To 100
              If Not FSO.FolderExists (strOutDir) Then
                  FSO.CreateFolder strOutDir
              End If
              strInPath = strInDir & "\test.txt"
              strOutPath = strOutDir & "\test" & irow & ".txt"
              Outputsheet.Cells(irow, 2) = "Started Copy File " & strInPath & " to " & strOutPath

              FSO.CopyFile "C:\Temp\In\FilesUpdated.txt", "C:\Temp\Out\FilesUpdated.txt", True

              FSO.CopyFile strInPath, strOutPath, True
              Outputsheet.Cells(irow, 3) = "Done: Country= " & Outputsheet.Cells(irow, 29)
              Outputsheet.Cells(irow, 2) = "Finished Copy File " & strInPath & " to " & strOutPath
          Next
          ' Example of CopyFolder
          FSO.CopyFolder "C:\Temp\In\dir1", "C:\Temp\Out\dir1", True

          ' It might be in use, so save it under a different name.
          ' Convert date and time to a string.
          strNow = "" & _
                   (Year(Now)   * 10000000000 _
                  + Month(Now)  * 100000000 _
                  + Day(Now)    * 1000000 _
                  + Hour(Now)   * 10000 _
                  + Minute(Now) * 100 _
                  + Second(Now))
          strSavePath = FSO.GetParentFolderName(wb.FullName ) & _
                    "\" & FSO.GetBaseName(wb.FullName ) & _
                    "_" & Left(strNow, 8) & "_" & Right(strNow, 6) & _
                    "." & FSO.GetExtensionName(wb.FullName)
          ' Save as a different name.
          wb.SaveAs strSavePath
      End Sub
    ]]></script>
    <script language="JScript"><![CDATA[
        // We use try-catch-finally just to display the sheet in case of an error.
        try {
           RunVBProcess();
        } catch(e) {
            WScript.Echo("Error[" + e.number + "]" + e.description);
        }
        finally {
            ExcelApp.Visible = true;
            // If you do not display it, the Excel process will be terminated with Quit.
            // ExcelApp.Quit();
            WScript.Quit(0);
        }
    ]]></script>
  </job>
</package>

VBSSample.bat

cscript //Nologo VBSSample.wsf
pause

I hope this is helpful.

[Addendum] If you choose not to display it, you need to end the Excel process with Quit, so I added a comment in the JScript.

@Metal, I mentioned it in the comments, but since it's hard to understand, I'll write it here.

This is how to make a batch file pause for input when using xcopy.Please add it at the end of the batch file.

set INPUT=
:ENTRY
set /p INPUT=Press 'y' to exit
if /i "%INPUT%" neq "y" goto :ENTRY
